title: INT8 stability orchestration and runtime kernel adaptor
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build an end-to-end orchestration pipeline and runtime adaptor that enables safer deployment of activation-aware INT8 quantized models (activation balancing approach) across Redwood’s serving runtime. This ticket covers: calibration workflow automation, per-batch and per-layer scale transfer, CI validation harness for accuracy regression detection, and lightweight kernel adaptor that provides graceful fallback to FP16/quant-degraded paths when runtime invariants are violated.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration pipeline produces per-layer scale maps and a deployable quant profile for target model families (GPT-like and encoder-only) without manual steps
CI gate that runs a representative eval suite detects top-line accuracy regression >0.6% and blocks rollout
Runtime kernel adaptor can switch between INT8 optimized kernel and fallback kernel with <8ms extra latency on p95 for 2K token requests
End-to-end rolling rollout (canary -> ramp) documented and validated in staging; rollback path automatable
Integration tests and benchmark dashboards show token cost reduction vs FP16 for typical chat workloads
design_notes: Use a two-stage calibration: (1) offline per-layer activation statistics collection with synthetic and sampled production traces; (2) constrained optimizer to compute per-channel rescale factors and final quant clipping thresholds
Prefer storing quant profiles as versioned artifacts in S3 with a strong naming convention: model@sha:quant-profile:v{semver}-activation-aware
Kernel adaptor is a thin layer that exposes an API to the runtime: select_kernel(model, profile, runtime_metrics) -> {int8_kernel|fallback_kernel}, with metrics hooks for decision making
Keep accuracy validation independent from engineering metrics: separate eval cluster that runs full eval sets (QA prompts, translation sets, and hallucination tests) to quantify semantic drift
Calibration should minimize cross-layer amplification of activation scales by solving a constrained least-squares for scale transfers (avoid heuristics unless necessary)
implementation_plan: Calibrator service: Python microservice to ingest activation traces and produce quant profiles (PR: github.com/redwood/quant-calib/pull/204)
CI harness: add a new job in runtime-acceptance to run quantized vs baseline on 3 canonical models and emit accuracy deltas and perf metrics
Kernel adaptor: implement C++ shim in runtime that can load two kernel binaries and do hot-swap on a per-request basis; add a health-check channel to revert to fallback on cache/overflow anomalies
Artifact storage: profile uploader that registers artifacts in model-registry with policy + immutability
Docs + runbook: write a deployment runbook for SREs that includes canary thresholds and rollback steps
testing_plan: Unit tests for calibrator math (edge cases: zero-variance activations, outliers)
Integration tests: serve quantized model in staging with synthetic traces and compare token-level logits with baseline FP16; assert topk agreement and perplexity thresholds
Regression suite: run semantic eval (QA + summarization) with golden prompts; block merges when accuracy delta > 0.6%
Performance tests: measure p50/p95 latency and throughput for small chat (256 tokens) and long context (2048 tokens) workloads
Fault injection: force KV cache flush and kernel OOM path to validate graceful fallback and unharmed in-flight responses
rollout_plan: Stage 0: internal staging – run 100% traffic for synthetic traces only, validate metrics for 24h
Stage 1: canary – 1% production traffic for 6 hours; monitor accuracy-sentinel and p95 latency
Stage 2: ramp – 10% -> 50% over 48h if no regressions; create automated rollback if accuracy delta exceeds threshold
Stage 3: full rollout – enable for customer tier lower than enterprise; schedule enterprise opt-in after 2 weeks
Rollback: immediate switch to fallback_kernel + mark profile as quarantined in model registry
metrics: p95_latency_ms — must not increase > 10% vs current kernel for INT8 path
cost_per_token_usd — expected decrease vs FP16 for steady-state chat workloads
fallback_rate — percentage of requests that used fallback_kernel; target < 0.5%
canary_blocked — boolean if CI/regression thresholds triggered
risks: Activation outliers may cause sporadic accuracy regressions not captured by sampling; mitigated by heavy tail sampling and fallback path
Kernel incompatibility across GPU types (some microkernels optimized for A100 might underperform on H100); mitigate by per-hardware profiling and hardware-tagged profiles
Latency spikes during hot-swap if fallback path loads large kernel binary; prefetch kernels into memory in canary
Operator error during rollout; mitigate through automated rollback and a one-click SRE runbook
